method: Read the assigned ITEMs (PQ-007 dcat/admin form endpoints, PQ-008 ApiHook SSRF), the upstream shared guidance and team4 auditor skills, then traced every claim to the current working tree (controller, vendor dcat-admin code, route/middleware registration, storage/Flysystem, nginx + Dockerfile deployment shape). MODE=static: no HTTP request, payload, queue run or container action was performed. No .env value or secret was printed; only key presence and file:line references are reported.
guidance_consumed: tools/php-audit-skills/shared/sink_definitions.md (#1 dynamic invocation / object instantiation, #4 file write, #6 SSRF)
environment_notes: Host has no php binary and MODE=static, so no runtime probe, queue run or HTTP request was made; PHP-wrapper/Flysystem behaviour statements are limited to what the source shows.

conf/php.ini contains no allow_url_fopen / open_basedir / disable_functions directive (grep: no match), so the shipped image keeps PHP defaults and the http/https/gopher/dict stream wrappers are available.

Queue is real: .env.example:36 QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis, config/queue.php:16 default env('QUEUE_CONNECTION','sync'), conf/supervisord.conf runs 'php /app/artisan queue:work --tries=3' as user application.

Deployment shape matters for PQ-007: Dockerfile:19-23 copies the tree then 'chown -R root:root /app' and only hands /app/storage, /app/bootstrap/cache, /app/public/uploads to the application user; both nginx configs (conf/default.conf, conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf) deny .php execution under /uploads/ and /storage/; no 'artisan storage:link' call exists in Dockerfile/conf/start.sh/conf/start-hook.sh.

findings.title: Dcat admin generic form endpoints instantiate and invoke a request-chosen class (_form_): dcat-api routes skip the admin.permission check and every Form::authorize() in this tree returns true, so any admin-panel account can drive any Form handler (incl. the vendor's extension-install form)
findings.sink_type: object_instantiation + arbitrary method invocation on an attacker-named class (sink_definitions.md #1 Dynamic Invocation)
findings.source: POST /admin/dcat-api/form (route name dcat.admin.dcat-api.form) body parameter '_form_' (Dcat\Admin\Widgets\Form::REQUEST_NAME, vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Widgets/Form.php:104), read verbatim at HandleFormController.php:100.
findings.sink: HandleFormController::resolveForm() -> class_exists($formClass) (line 102) -> app($formClass) (line 107) -> method_exists($form,'handle') (line 109); the caller then runs $form->passesAuthorization() (line 22), $form->form() (26), $form->validate($request) (28), $form->sanitize($request->all()) (32) and $form->handle($input) (34).
findings.reachability: Route registration: vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Admin.php:614-631 builds the dcat-api group with prefix admin_base_path('dcat-api') and 'middleware' => config('admin.route.middleware'); config/admin.php:67-77 sets that to ['web','admin','admin.force-password'] and config/admin.php:70 the prefix to 'admin'. The 'admin' group (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/AdminServiceProvider.php:79-88) starts with 'admin.auth' => Dcat\Admin\Http\Middleware\Authenticate, so an /admin session is required (CORRECTLY protected against unauthenticated access). What is NOT enforced: (a) the dcat ACL - Dcat\Admin\Http\Middleware\Permission::shouldPassThrough() returns true for every dcat-api route because isApiRoute() matches routeIs(admin_api_route_name('*')) = 'dcat.admin.dcat-api.*' (Permission.php:83-86 and 94-97), and (b) form-level authorization - HandleFormController.php:22 calls $form->passesAuthorization(), which resolves to Dcat\Admin\Traits\HasAuthorization::authorize() whose default body is 'return true;' (HasAuthorization.php:16-19 and 27-30); 'grep -rn "function authorize" app vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src' shows the only definitions are that default plus Console stub templates, so ImportCarmis/SystemSetting/EmailTest/InstallFromLocal all pass. CSRF is still required ('web' group -> app/Http/Middleware/VerifyCsrfToken.php:21-26 only exempts pay/*/notify_url and pay/*/return_url).
findings.preconditions: 1) A session for any account on the dcat admin guard (config/admin.php:130-152 guard 'admin'), including a non-super-admin Administrator that has NO role/permission rows - the ACL never runs for dcat-api routes. 2) A valid CSRF token from an admin page (or a same-origin admin-context script). 3) For the RCE branch, base_path('dcat-admin-extensions') (config/admin.php:362-366) must be writable by the PHP user - the shipped Dockerfile leaves /app root:root, so that branch fails in the shipped image.
findings.impact: Any autoloadable class that satisfies class_exists + app() + method_exists('handle') can be driven, and the working tree's Form subclasses make this a concrete privilege-model bypass for multi-account panels: (a) App\Admin\Forms\SystemSetting::handle() does Cache::put('system-setting', $input) (app/Admin/Forms/SystemSetting.php:18-24) with fully attacker-shaped input, and that cache IS the site configuration (dujiaoka_config_get() in app/Helpers/functions.php:58-62; MailConfigService::apply() reads host/username/password/from_* from it; BaseController::render() uses 'template' at app/Http/Controllers/BaseController.php:28-32) -> an account with zero permissions can rewrite site config and SMTP credentials and blank out every key it does not send; (b) App\Admin\Forms\ImportCarmis::handle() runs Carmis::query()->insert($carmisData) and Storage::disk('public')->get()/delete() on attacker paths (app/Admin/Forms/ImportCarmis.php:20-55); (c) App\Admin\Forms\EmailTest::handle() sends arbitrary mail through the app's SMTP (app/Admin/Forms/EmailTest.php:27-49); (d) the vendor's Dcat\Admin\Http\Forms\InstallFromLocal is a full extension-install primitive: handle() unzips an attacker archive and calls $manager->extract($path,true)->load()->update() (InstallFromLocal.php:15-51) while Extend\Manager::loadExtension/resolveExtension does 'new $serviceProvider($this->app)' with the class name taken from the archive's composer.json extra.dcat-admin (Manager.php:212-251) -> arbitrary PHP class instantiation = RCE when the extension directory is writable. In the shipped image the last step is blocked by file ownership (Dockerfile:19-23), so the RCE branch is 'blocked-by-deployment', not 'impossible'.
findings.evidence: EVID_SOURCE: vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Http/Controllers/HandleFormController.php:96-113 - 'if (! $request->has(Form::REQUEST_NAME)) ... $formClass = $request->get(Form::REQUEST_NAME); if (! class_exists($formClass)) ... $form = app($formClass); if (! method_exists($form, 'handle')) ...' (no instanceof Dcat\Admin\Widgets\Form / Dcat\Admin\Form check, no class allowlist, no namespace restriction). EVID_SINK: same file :34 'return $this->sendResponse($form->handle($input));' with $input = $form->sanitize($request->all()) at :32. EVID_ROUTE: vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Admin.php:617-628 (prefix admin_base_path('dcat-api'), middleware config('admin.route.middleware'), names 'dcat-api.'+form/upload/destroy-file) and app/Admin/routes.php:7 Admin::routes(). EVID_ACL_BYPASS: vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Http/Middleware/Permission.php:83-86 'return $request->routeIs(admin_api_route_name('*'));' + :94-97 'if ($this->isApiRoute($request) || ...) { return true; }' and vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Support/helpers.php:417-419 admin_api_route_name() = prefix 'dcat.admin.dcat-api.'. EVID_AUTHZ_DEFAULT: vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Traits/HasAuthorization.php:16-30 (passesAuthorization -> authorize -> 'return true;'), no authorize() override under app/. EVID_GADGET_EXTENSION_INSTALL: vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Http/Forms/InstallFromLocal.php:15-51 + :53-60 (form defines file('extension')->required()->disk('local')) and vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Extend/Manager.php:348-392 (Zip::extract -> checkFiles -> copyDirectory to admin_extension_path(name)) + :234-251 ('$serviceProvider = new $serviceProvider($this->app);'). EVID_WRITE_BLOCKER: Dockerfile:17-23 ('chown -R root:root /app', only storage/cache/uploads to application) and config/admin.php:365 'dir' => base_path('dcat-admin-extensions'). EVID_EXECUTION_RESPONSE: [Not obtained - MODE=static, no request/container executed].
findings.false_positive_counter_check: Rule 8 analysis: (i) Not pre-auth - the route carries 'admin'/'admin.auth', config('admin.auth.except') is only ['auth/login','auth/logout'] (config/admin.php:156-159) and Authenticate::shouldPassThrough() matches by route name/path, which 'admin/dcat-api/form' does not (Dcat\Admin\Http\Middleware\Authenticate.php:36-58). (ii) CSRF applies. (iii) On a default install with a single super-admin there is no privilege boundary to cross, which is why this is not rated critical; the rating reflects the multi-account case where the dcat ACL is the only boundary and it is bypassed. (iv) The instantiation itself is not an unrestricted gadget: the container must be able to build the class and the flow needs passesAuthorization()+form()+validate()+sanitize()+handle(), so in practice only Form-compatible classes reach a sink; I found no zero-arg constructor gadget that acts on its own, so no claim is made about constructor-only abuse. (v) The RCE branch is defeated by the shipped image's ownership of /app, so it is reported as an environment-dependent escalation rather than a shipped webshell.
findings.remediation: 1) In resolveForm() add a hard type gate before app(): require is_subclass_of($formClass, \Dcat\Admin\Widgets\Form::class) (or Form\Form) AND an explicit per-class allowlist of renderable forms (dcat supports $form->passesAuthorization() but defaults to true), e.g. map a signed/opaque form id to a fixed class instead of trusting a FQCN from the request. 2) Do not let dcat-api routes bypass the ACL for state-changing forms: extend Permission::shouldPassThrough() or add a route-level 'admin.permission:<method>' to /admin/dcat-api/form*, or re-check $user->allPermissions() inside HandleFormController. 3) Override authorize() in every App\Admin\Forms\* handler with a real permission check (or set an explicit ACL on the routes that render them: /admin/system-setting, /admin/import-carmis, /admin/email-test). 4) Remove the vendor InstallFromLocal form from the reachable set (or gate it behind a super-admin check) and keep dcat-admin-extensions non-writable by the PHP user. 5) Upgrade to a dcat/laravel-admin release that adds the type/alloylist check in HandleFormController.

findings.title: POST /admin/dcat-api/form/upload accepts any file type for a request-chosen form field (accept('txt') is client-side only) and never calls passesAuthorization()
findings.verdict: confirmed code path (static) / blocked by the shipped nginx+filesystem layout
findings.sink_type: file write (sink_definitions.md #4 move_uploaded_file/putFileAs) + missing authorization on the upload variant
findings.source: multipart POST /admin/dcat-api/form/upload with params upload_column|_column (field name), _id (mandatory, UploadField.php:185-189), _form_ (form class) and the file part '_file_' (Dcat\Admin\Support\WebUploader::FILE_NAME, WebUploader.php:21/37).
findings.sink: HandleFormController::uploadFile() :37-44 -> resolveForm() -> getField() (:51-73, $column = $this->uploader()->upload_column ?: $request->get('_column')) -> $form->field($column)->upload($this->file()) ; final write is Illuminate\Filesystem\FilesystemAdapter::putFileAs via Dcat\Admin\Form\Field\UploadField::upload() (UploadField.php:181-221, name resolved at :195/:120-139, write at :206-208).
findings.reachability: Same route group as PQ-007 (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Admin.php:627) => requires an authenticated admin session + CSRF, and is NOT covered by the dcat ACL (Permission.php:83-97). No passesAuthorization() call exists in uploadFile() (contrast HandleFormController.php:22 in handle()); with the current tree that omission has no extra effect because every Form uses the default authorize()=>true, so it is a latent library defect, not an add-on here. Which file lands where is decided by the form class + field: App\Admin\Forms\ImportCarmis::form() declares $this->file('carmis_txt')->disk('public')->uniqueName()->accept('txt')->maxSize(5120) (app/Admin/Forms/ImportCarmis.php:69-74). accept() only fills client-side webuploader options (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Form/Field/WebUploader.php:20-31), so the server-side rule set is just ['max:5120'] (WebUploader::maxSize -> rules('max:...') at :72-78), evaluated by UploadField::getValidationErrors() (UploadField.php:343-368, Arr::set($rules, $this->column, $fieldRules) -> Validator) => no mime/extension rule at all.
findings.preconditions: 1) Admin session + CSRF (as above). 2) The requested _column must exist in the chosen form (otherwise field() returns null and the request 500s at HandleFormController.php:43). 3) The uploaded blob is stored with the client-supplied extension, but only under the field's disk root: the shipped Dockerfiles do not run 'artisan storage:link' and both nginx configs deny .php under /uploads/ and /storage/, so no webshell in the shipped image.
findings.impact: An authenticated admin-panel account can place a file with an arbitrary extension and arbitrary bytes into /app/storage/app/files/ (public disk, via the ImportCarmis field) or /app/public/uploads/{files,images}/ (admin disk, uploads are web-served). Name is md5(uniqid()).<client extension> for uniqueName() fields, or the raw client filename otherwise. Confirmed consequences: arbitrary content becomes web-served (HTML/SVG under /uploads/ => same-origin stored XSS; the ImportCarmis field's 'accept txt' restriction is decorative); the same class list lets destroy-file (:75-86 -> UploadField::deleteFile(), UploadField.php:402-426) delete any path inside the chosen disk root. Direct code execution is prevented in the shipped deployment by conf/default.conf and conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf ('location ~ \.php$ { deny all; }' inside /uploads/ and /storage/) and by the missing storage symlink - it becomes RCE on a stock Laravel nginx vhost (no deny rule) or once an operator adds storage:link.
findings.evidence: EVID_FILE_WRITE_PATH: HandleFormController.php:37-44 (no passesAuthorization) + :53 '$column = $this->uploader()->upload_column ?: $request->get('_column');' + :56 '$form->field($column)' + :43 '->upload($this->file())'. EVID_PATH_CONSTRUCTION: UploadField.php:195 '$this->name = $this->getStoreName($file);' -> :120-139 (uniqueName => md5(uniqid()).'.'.$file->getClientOriginalExtension()) -> :206-208 putFileAs($this->getDirectory(), $file, $this->name), directory from :152 defaultDirectory() = config('admin.upload.directory.file')='files'. EVID_VALIDATION_GAP: app/Admin/Forms/ImportCarmis.php:69-74 (accept('txt') / maxSize(5120) only) + Form/Field/WebUploader.php:20-31 (accept writes $this->options['accept'], i.e. the JS widget config, not $this->rules) + UploadField.php:352-368 (only getRules() are validated) => extension/mime unrestricted server-side. EVID_WEB_EXPOSURE_BLOCKED: conf/default.conf:'location ^~ /uploads/ {... location ~ \.php$ { deny all; } try_files $uri =404; }' and the identical 'location ^~ /storage/' block in conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf; config/filesystems.php disks 'public' root storage_path('app/public') with url /storage and 'admin' root public_path('uploads'); no storage:link in Dockerfile / conf/start.sh / conf/start-hook.sh (grep: no match). EVID_EXECUTION_RESPONSE: [Not obtained - MODE=static, no upload performed].
findings.false_positive_counter_check: Rule 8 analysis: (a) passesAuthorization() is indeed missing from uploadFile(), but since every Form in this tree inherits authorize()=>true (HasAuthorization.php:27-30), the skip does not grant anything extra today - reported as a latent defect, not as the primary impact. (b) Directory traversal out of the disk root was checked and rejected: destroyFile()/handle() pass user paths straight to Storage::disk()->delete()/get(), and Laravel 12 FileSystemManager::createLocalDriver wraps the adapter in League\Flysystem\Filesystem (vendor/laravel/framework/.../FilesystemManager.php:354-375) whose WhitespacePathNormalizer throws PathTraversalDetected on a leading '..' (vendor/league/flysystem/src/WhitespacePathNormalizer.php:33-51), so writes/reads/deletes stay inside storage/app or public/uploads. (c) An executable upload into public/uploads is blocked twice: nginx denies .php there and the Image field that owns the admin disk carries $rules = ['nullable','image'] (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Form/Field/Image.php:52) whose shouldBlockPhpUpload()/mime guessing rejects php/php3/php4/php5/phtml/pht/phar. (d) Chunked-upload temp paths accept a raw '_id' (Support/WebUploader.php:235-237 -> storage_path('tmp').'/'.$path) but the merged file is only written when every expected .part file is already present in that directory (WebUploader.php:165-174, 193-216), so an attacker cannot create directories this way - downgraded to a hardening note. Net determination: genuine missing server-side content-type enforcement and a missing authorization call on the upload variant; impact limited to arbitrary-content files in web-served dirs by the shipped nginx deny rules.
findings.remediation: 1) Add a server-side rule in the field definitions, e.g. ->rules('mimes:txt,text/plain') or ->accept() should map to a Laravel mimes/extensions rule (patch Form/Field/WebUploader::accept to also push 'mimes:...'), and enable the same rule inside HandleFormController::uploadFile() for every field. 2) Call $form->passesAuthorization() (and a real authorize() override) in uploadFile() and destroyFile(), matching handle(). 3) Restrict getField() to File/Image/MultipleFile instances and require the column to be declared by the form (reject unknown _column). 4) Keep the nginx 'deny .php under /uploads and /storage' blocks (already added in this branch) and do not add a storage:link without them.

findings.title: SSRF: ApiHook job passes the admin-editable goods.api_hook value straight to file_get_contents() (no scheme/host/IP allowlist), from the queue worker, with order PII in the body
findings.verdict: confirmed code path (static) / second-order, admin precondition
findings.source: goods.api_hook, written only through the Dcat goods form textarea (app/Admin/Controllers/GoodsController.php:155, no ->rules()/validation), read back in the job via $this->goodsService->detail($this->order->goods_id) (app/Jobs/ApiHook.php:60).
findings.reachability: app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:452 'ApiHook::dispatch($order)' is executed unconditionally after DB::commit() when an order is completed, so any path that completes an order (payment notify/return, manual processing, re-check) triggers it. The job runs in the worker (conf/supervisord.conf program:dujiaoka-worker, 'php /app/artisan queue:work --tries=3'; .env.example:36 QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis), i.e. a different network position than the customer. The target URL is NOT attacker-controlled at trigger time: goods writes are behind config/admin.php:74 ['web','admin','admin.force-password'] and app/Admin/routes.php:13.
findings.preconditions: 1) Someone who can write the goods row sets api_hook to a URL (admin panel, or DB/backup tampering). 2) The goods is ordered and the order completes. 3) allow_url_fopen stays enabled (conf/php.ini has no allow_url_fopen/open_basedir/disable_functions directive). Default installs are unaffected: the column has no default and ApiHook.php:62 returns early on empty().
findings.impact: The worker issues an attacker-chosen POST with a JSON body to any URL the DB holds: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/, http://169.254.169.254/ (cloud metadata), docker bridge service names, and - because the string is used verbatim - wrapper schemes such as gopher://host:port/_<encoded> or dict://, which in PHP let you speak raw bytes to an internal TCP service (Redis/MySQL/etc.); the shipped compose stack keeps Redis/MySQL inside the container/stack. The body also carries order title, order_sn, customer email, actual_price and free-form order info (ApiHook.php:65-74), so a plain http:// target exfiltrates customer PII in cleartext. The response is discarded (line 85 assignment-free), so the SSRF is blind.
findings.evidence: EVID_SSRF_FINAL_URL: app/Jobs/ApiHook.php:60-64 (goodsService->detail + empty() guard) and :84-85 ($context = stream_context_create($opts); file_get_contents($goodInfo->api_hook, false, $context)) - the DB value is the URL, verbatim. EVID_SSRF_URL_NORMALIZATION: no validation anywhere on the path - GoodsController.php:155 '$form->textarea('api_hook');' (no rules), app/Models/Goods.php has no mutator, GoodsService::detail() is a plain Eloquent lookup, and grep over app/ shows only GoodsController.php:123,155 and ApiHook.php:62,85 reference api_hook. No filter_var/FILTER_VALIDATE_URL, no scheme allowlist, no resolved-IP private-range check, no redirect restriction exists in ApiHook.php (whole file 87 lines). EVID_SSRF_EGRESS: ApiHook.php:65-74 body fields + :77-83 POST/JSON context => data leaves the process to the chosen host. EVID_TRIGGER: app/Service/OrderProcessService.php:452. EVID_EXECUTION_RESPONSE: [Not obtained - MODE=static, no queue worker/container started, no payload sent].
findings.false_positive_counter_check: Rule 8 analysis: (a) This is second-order: an anonymous customer cannot choose the URL, only cause a request to an already configured one (grep shows no non-admin write path to goods.api_hook; Goods has no mass-assignment hole). (b) The response body never returns to an HTTP client, so no internal-data disclosure path - only blind interaction/egress. (c) file:// or php://filter in api_hook cannot disclose anything because the return value is discarded and the job ends at line 85 (rejected as LFI below). (d) CRLF/header injection is impossible: headers are the static literal at :80 and the body is json_encode()d at :81. (e) The queue worker does not run with elevated containers privileges and the sink has a 30s job timeout (ApiHook.php:28). Net determination: real missing-control defect (unvalidated outbound URL + PII egress + raw-wrapper SSRF), kept at medium because of the admin precondition and the blind response.
findings.remediation: 1) Validate on write: ->rules('nullable|url:http,https') plus a server-side check that rejects non-https, userinfo, loopback/link-local/RFC1918 (after DNS resolution) and unexpected ports. 2) In app/Jobs/ApiHook.php replace the raw stream wrapper with an HTTP client that pins the resolved IP, disallows cross-host redirects, sets connect/read timeouts, and allowlists the scheme (https only) so gopher:// + dict:// disappear. 3) Keep a config allowlist of webhook hosts instead of free text, and send only order_sn plus a signed token so customer email/order_info are not shipped in cleartext. 4) Apply the same hardening to the sibling sinks app/Jobs/BarkPush.php (bark_server/bark_token) and app/Jobs/ServerJiang.php (token concatenated into the URL path).

rejected.title: Unauthenticated (pre-auth) access to /admin/dcat-api/form, /form/upload, /form/destroy-file, /action, /value, /render, /editor-md/upload, /tinymce/upload
rejected.reason: Rejected: the dcat-api group is registered with 'middleware' => config('admin.route.middleware') (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/src/Admin.php:617-621) and config/admin.php:67-77 sets ['web','admin','admin.force-password']; the 'admin' group (AdminServiceProvider.php:79-88) begins with 'admin.auth' (Dcat\Admin\Http\Middleware\Authenticate), which redirects guests to auth/login. The only pass-through list is config('admin.auth.except') = ['auth/login','auth/logout'] (config/admin.php:156-159) and Authenticate::shouldPassThrough() matches by route name or request path, neither of which matches 'admin/dcat-api/*'. config('admin.auth.enable') is true (config/admin.php:130). So every dcat-api endpoint needs a logged-in admin-guard session; the finding is an authorization/ACL bypass inside that boundary, not an auth bypass.

rejected.title: Constructor-only gadget abuse of app($formClass) (dangerous side effect at instantiation, before the handle() check)
rejected.reason: Rejected as unproven: app($formClass) at HandleFormController.php:107 does run before method_exists('handle') at :109, so an attacker-named class IS constructed. However the container must resolve every constructor argument (�scalars without defaults throw BindingResolutionException => 500) and I found no autoloadable class in app/ or vendor/ whose zero-arg-resolvable constructor performs a file/network/DB action on its own - the only classes whose instance methods reach a sink are the Form subclasses already covered by PQ-007. No concrete gadget => no separate finding (anti_hallucination Rule 1/3: not asserting behaviour that was not read in source).

rejected.title: Path traversal out of the storage root via destroyFile()'s 'key' parameter or the upload filename
rejected.reason: Rejected: user paths reach Storage::disk()->delete()/get() (HandleFormController.php:83 -> UploadField.php:402-426; ImportCarmis.php:27/50) but Laravel 12 wraps local adapters in League\Flysystem\Filesystem (vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Filesystem/FilesystemManager.php:354-375), whose WhitespacePathNormalizer rejects a leading '..' with PathTraversalDetected (vendor/league/flysystem/src/WhitespacePathNormalizer.php:33-51) - so paths stay inside storage_path('app/public') or public_path('uploads'). The stored name for uniqueName() fields is md5(uniqid()).<client extension> (UploadField.php:313-316), which cannot contain a directory separator. Chunked uploads take '_id' verbatim (Support/WebUploader.php:235-237) but only merge when every expected part file already exists in that directory (WebUploader.php:165-216), so it cannot be used to create arbitrary directories.

rejected.title: PHP webshell via the upload endpoint in the shipped deployment
rejected.reason: Rejected for the shipped image: (a) the only fields reachable with a request-chosen column that live on the web-served 'admin' disk are Image fields, and Dcat\Admin\Form\Field\Image::$rules = ['nullable','image'] (Image.php:52) makes Laravel's image/mimes validation reject php/php3/php4/php5/phtml/pht/phar (shouldBlockPhpUpload + content-based extension guessing); (b) the ImportCarmis file field writes to the 'public' disk (config/filesystems.php root storage_path('app/public')), which is only served through /storage and no 'artisan storage:link' is run by Dockerfile/conf/start.sh/conf/start-hook.sh (grep: no match); (c) both nginx configs deny .php below /uploads/ and /storage/ (conf/default.conf, conf/dujiaoka-nginx.conf). The remaining risk (arbitrary content/extension in web-served dirs on a stock vhost) is reported inside PQ-007-UPLOAD.

rejected.title: Local file read (LFI) through api_hook with file:// or php://filter
rejected.reason: Rejected: api_hook is not scheme-restricted, so file:///etc/passwd parses, but the return value of file_get_contents() is discarded (app/Jobs/ApiHook.php:85 is a bare call, the result is not assigned, echoed, logged or returned and the job has no code after it), so file content cannot reach any attacker-reachable channel. Kept only as part of the missing scheme/URL validation defect in PQ-008.

rejected.title: Stored XSS in the admin goods detail page through goods.api_hook (app/Admin/Controllers/GoodsController.php:123 unescape())
rejected.reason: The sink is real: app/Admin/Controllers/GoodsController.php:123 '$show->api_hook()->unescape()->as(function ($apiHook) { return ""; })' with $show->api_hook()->unescape() setting escape=false (Show\Field.php:510-530) and the view emitting '{!! $content !!}' when escape is false (vendor/dcat/laravel-admin/resources/views/show/field.blade.php:10-24), so a value like '' executes. But the only write path is the same admin-guarded goods form (GoodsController.php:155), so exploiting it means an admin attacking an admin (self-XSS on a single-account install; a restricted admin with goods-edit permission could target a super-admin on a multi-account install). Not reported as an injection finding of its own - it is an output-encoding hardening item (use the default escaping or htmlspecialchars the value) that belongs to the xss-csrf-session domain team, and the previous injection artifact in this repository reached the same conclusion.
